newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares rally 1.9 pct, index at 52-week high.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares rally 1.9 pct, index at 52-week high.

text.p: ** (0845 GMT) - Bombay stocks power ahead in delayed start
on the first day of new-account trade
** Bombay's benchmark 30-share index jumps 80.61 points, or
1.95 percent, to 4,213.85 minutes after opening
** Shares of HDFC, Hindustan Lever and ACC lead early
charge by bull operators
** Bombay stocks flirt at 52-week high levels - traders
** National exchange index up 14.0 points, or 1.20 pct
** BSES and TVS Suzuki due to announce 1996/97 results

Blue chips raced to a bullish start in delayed opening at the Bombay Stock Exchange on Monday, with a flurry of overseas buy orders pushing the benchmark index to new 52-week high levels, traders said.
"The market is booming. Multinational and cement stocks are in the limelight," said a dealer at a local institutional brokerage. "There seems to be some heavy delivery-based buying coming in."
Bombay's top 30-share index rose 80 points, or nearly two percent to 4213 minutes after opening.
A sharp rally by index-heavy weights -- Hindustan Lever rose 58.75 rupees at 1,443.0, ITC surged 27.75 rupees at 552.50 and MTNL gained 10.0 at 307.0 pushed the index higher, traders said.
"The market looks better. There is a sharp rise in select stocks," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs.
At 3.15 p.m. (0945 GMT) the Bombay index was up 96.71 points, or 2.34 percent, at 4,229.95.
Monday's sharp rally helped the index cross its old 52-week high of 4,153.80 scaled on Friday.
The blue chip gauge has already shown a handsome gain of 427 points, or nearly 12 percent in the last five weeks on the back of foreign fund buying.
Cement stocks which have been major underperformers notched up early gains due to the changing market outlook for the sector, traders said.

Shares of Associated Cement Companies rose 40.0 rupees to 1,430.0. Gujarat Ambuja Cement was up 17 rupees at 346.0 hitting new 52-week highs on market rumours about a possible bonus share issue by the company.

Shares of India's Housing Development & Finance Company (HDFC) jumped 371.0 rupees, or nearly ten percent to 4,08275 at the Bombay exchange after foreign funds turned buyers in the stock, traders said.
India's leading housing finance company said on Friday it had received central bank approval for foreign institutional investors (FIIs) to raise their holding limits to 30 percent from 24 percent.

Disbursals made by HDFC rose 24 percent so far in 1997/98 (April-March) to 3.23 billion rupees against 2.61 billion in the same period last year, HDFC Chairman Deepak Parekh said at the company's annual shareholders' meeting last week.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
